counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span identifies a specific glomerular etiology for the nephrotic syndrome.
No raw span links the single sildenafil dose to the nephrotic syndrome.
The acute creatinine rise from 1.9 to 3.7 mg/dL is not captured by the R3 label alone.
response.rationale: R3 is the only candidate whose raw spans cover the nephrotic triad (nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, 4+ protein) and best explains the generalized edema, weight gain, and pleural effusions. R1 captures only the creatinine trajectory and misses the nephrotic features; R5 has only eosinophilia plus AKI without a raw drug-exposure link and is contradicted by the bland sediment; R6 and R8 are single-comorbidity associations.

rejected.why: Only eosinophilia and AKI; no raw span for drug exposure, and bland sediment with scant WBCs does not support AIN; does not explain nephrotic-range proteinuria or hypoalbuminemia.
Only the comorbidity 'hypertension'; cannot explain acute edema, nephrotic proteinuria, or AKI.
Only long-term allopurinol use; no raw evidence of allopurinol-induced injury or temporal link to the acute presentation.
Correlated restatement of R1 with the same creatinine spans; the temporal modifier adds no independent raw support beyond R1.
